title: Reduce selected compiler height 47.1× with a checked net-tax application
body:
## Summary

Reduce #6030's sufficient log2-rank from 65,807,000,000,000 to 1,397,200,000,000 (~47.1x), retaining its complete invoice and κ=0.003125804. The original merged-only #4480 application at H=1,449,000,000,000 remains independently reproducible.

The optional example applies the separately verified [sharp-net theorem](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a0ef8b7ae2592202247b15da453ce42598863a26/research/sharp-net-splitting-tax): N<=1937/250000 permits v=366,p=36,h=6400. Against a retuned old-coefficient certificate at H=1,433,600,000,000, the added improvement is exactly 13/512 (2.5390625%). The pending theorem and its proof are explicitly pinned and exported.

Credit #4433/#4480, #5787 and #6109. Base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a; audited #6030 source: 772dd10a5859a1d15f4851feb371519789213ad8.

## Evidence

```sh
python3 -I -W error -B research/selected6030-smaller-compiler/joint_verify.py
```

Expected: PASS_SELECTED6030_OPTIONAL_SHARP_NET. Eight registered normal/optimized and read-only portable checks pass. Separate interval and binomial/Newton engines verify the coefficient bound and all 38+37 polynomial coefficients. Full completion is charged; preceding-rank controls reject and all 54+4 outer checks pass. Controls detect understated coefficients, wrong root brackets, omitted paid tails and insufficient product/degree.

## Limitations and next questions

No new κ. This reduces a sufficient rank exponent, not runtime, and makes no global-optimality claim. Five framework assumptions remain; the huge word and precision schedule are not materialized. Fresh finite constants must be counted. Full-history validation was unavailable in the shallow checkout.

## Attribution

@CubeJerry, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; predecessor notices retained. [Proofs, pins and reviews](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/223ea940b604c1f8a2bd28093618628ba4a113a4/research/selected6030-smaller-compiler). No human or proof-kernel acceptance claimed.
